note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on.

compliance.verdict: Mostly sound but not yet fully compliant: three findings survive, one medium (the band-pass band edges and width the instruction fixes are not checked) and two low. The rest of the item holds up. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates (exit 0, ~80 s). All gates pass and gates.json is identical to the author's: solvability 10/10, size 711 tokens, variants 4/4 at V5, start fails first at V2 as expected, and 16 valid mutants all killed. Split discipline holds: the seed channels/demo_quantization.grc is a dev seed and the task is dev, with sha256 23f35aa3... matching both the example file and the split file. id, directory and split agree, and no other item uses this cluster. licence, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, fault (nonexistent_block, V2), level L2 (9 functional blocks, filtering) and disjointness (nothing in training_task_specs.json involves quantization) are compliant. The perturbation record matches the original example (100000 / 16 / -150 / -150 / samp_rate*1.0247385/11.0 / samp_rate/11.0 / samp_rate/2). Importing build.py without its save step regenerates task.json, reference.grc, start.grc and all 4 variants byte-identically, with no schema errors. The canary appears only in task.json. The quoted GRC error text matches GRC FlowGraph.py exactly. All 16 mutations are spec-breaking, reach V4 and are killed by the checks their 'breaks' labels name. The oracle is robust to the noise seed: over 400 seeds every check passes, and seed 0 with absolute file paths and an Embedded-Python rounding quantizer also pass the real ladder. Floor and truncation quantizers are rejected. The findings: (F1, medium) a filter narrowed to 6-14 kHz, shifted edges (7-18, 5-18 kHz) and a 1 kHz transition width all pass V5, although spec_properties claims the 6-18 kHz band is checked; (F2, low) an off-spec mid-rise quantizer passes, so the claimed rounding to multiples of 1/32 is not verified; (F3, low) leaving the Missing Block disabled in the graph is accepted by GRC but failed at V2, and the instruction does not say it must be removed. Scratch work is in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-08 and C:\Users\Lenovo\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Lenovo-Documents--MScAC-2701-ml-ops-project-project\e3a3c780-e6be-4b4a-8abe-931944b53353\scratchpad\rev08. The task directory was not modified apart from the requested gates re-run, which rewrote gates.json with identical content.

findings.claim: The oracle does not check the band-pass filter's band edges or transition width. The instruction states them ('the band from 6 kHz to 18 kHz (Hann window, 2.4 kHz transition width)', 'Keep ... the band-pass filter ... as they are'), and spec_properties.noise_band claims 'band-pass filtered to 6-18 kHz' is checked. In practice, an answer whose filter passes 6-14 kHz, 7-18 kHz or 5-18 kHz, or has a 1 kHz transition width, passes V5.
findings.evidence: I applied set_param edits to reference.grc and ran ladder.check with task.json; every one of these reached V5 with all checks passing: band_pass_filter_0 high_cutoff_freq=14000, 15000 or 16000; low_cutoff_freq=7000 or 5000; width=1000 (a Hamming window also passes, but that is not measurable). The only noise-band check is p2p band_fraction 7.5-11.5 kHz, which covers the passband below the tone. The f2p 0-4 / 20-24 kHz floor checks only catch noise that leaks more than 2 kHz outside the band. With high_cutoff=14 kHz the total RMS falls only ~1.5% (window +-5%) and the 7.5-11.5 kHz share rises ~3% (window +-10%). None of the 16 mutations narrows the band, so the mutation gate could not expose this. Measured on the reference over 200 noise seeds, with the effect of each filter error: upper-passband share 13.7-16.6 kHz = 0.0221, rel. std 3.6%; hi=16k gives -36%, hi=15k -70%. Transition-band shares 4.8-7.2 and 16.8-19.2 kHz = 0.0059 each, rel. std about 4.4%; lo=7k gives -75%, lo=5k +111%, hi=17k -75%, width 1k +31%.
findings.suggested_fix: Add p2p checks tied to the stated filter. One is band_fraction 13.7-16.6 kHz on 'out' (expect ~0.0221, i.e. 0.1^2*2.9/24/P_TOT, +-10%), which checks the upper passband above the tone. Another is band_fraction over the two transition bands 4.8-7.2 kHz and 16.8-19.2 kHz (expect ~0.0059 each, computed from the reference filter response, tolerance about +-30% so that a 1 kHz edge error fails). Add mutations such as {set_param band_pass_filter_0 high_cutoff_freq 15000, breaks noise_band} and {set_param low_cutoff_freq 7000}. Pooling 7.5-11.5 and 13.7-16.6 kHz also narrows the seed spread of the noise-level check from 2.7% to 2.3% rel. std. Today the 7.5-11.5 kHz check ranges 0.0284-0.0332 over 400 seeds against a 0.02745-0.03355 window, about 3.3 sigma of margin.

findings.claim: The core f2p requirement is only partly verified. The instruction requires every sample to be rounded to the nearest multiple of 1/32, with codes.dat holding the integer quantization levels; the oracle checks only the power of the rounding-noise floor. A mid-rise quantizer, which outputs odd multiples of 1/64 so that codes.dat holds half-integers, passes every check. spec_properties.six_bit_floor nonetheless says 'quantized.dat is rounded to multiples of 1/32' is checked.
findings.evidence: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-08/C_midrise.grc is the start graph with the missing block replaced by Multiply 32 -> Add Const -0.5 -> Float To Short -> Short To Float -> Add Const 0.5 -> Multiply 1/32. Through ./gb ladder with task.json it reaches V5 with all 7 checks passing: floor shares 2.50e-4 / 2.54e-4, codes RMS 7.509, out RMS 0.2346, peak 12600 Hz, noise share 0.0298. A numpy sweep on 40 seeds gives the same result (mid-rise 40/40 pass). Floor and truncation quantizers are correctly rejected (0/40).
findings.suggested_fix: Either add an oracle feature that tests the lattice, for example the share of codes.dat samples within 1e-4 of an integer (expect 1.0), or max |x - rint(x)| on codes.dat (expect 0, tol 1e-4), together with a mid-rise mutant. Or reword spec_properties.six_bit_floor and its checked_by so they claim only the 6-bit noise-floor level, not rounding to multiples of 1/32, and record the gap for team review.

findings.claim: The task fails a repair that GNU Radio Companion itself accepts. The repair adds a correct channels_quantizer and leaves the original 'quantizer' (id blocks_quantizer_ff) in the file, disabled and unconnected. GRC 3.10.12 validates and generates this graph, but the ladder fails it at V2. The instruction asks only to 'repair the flowgraph so that it works as described'; it does not say the Missing Block must be removed. That requirement appears only in spec_properties.loads.
findings.evidence: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-08/D_dummy_disabled.grc: ./gb ladder reports first_failed V2 with "unknown block id 'blocks_quantizer_ff' (block 'quantizer')". Loading the same file through the GRC platform gives fg.is_valid() True with no error messages, and the Generator writes the Python file. GRC's FlowGraph.import_data comments that errors of disabled blocks are not displayed, and DummyBlock.enabled is always False. For comparison, start.grc is invalid in GRC ('Port is not connected'). This is ladder policy rather than something specific to this task, but this nonexistent_block repair is where it most plausibly bites.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one clause to the instruction, for example 'the repaired flowgraph should not contain any Missing Block', which leaks nothing about the fix. Alternatively, document at harness level that V2 rejects unknown block ids even in disabled blocks, and note it in the review notes.

item-quality.verdict: Mostly sound, but fix F1 before acceptance. Confirmed correct: the seed channels/demo_quantization.grc is in the dev split and its sha256 matches; the perturbations match the original example; the level (L2: 9 functional blocks with filtering) and family (repair) are right. The fault is realistic: the start graph fails at V2 for the stated reason, and the quoted GRC message 'Block id "blocks_quantizer_ff" not found.' matches GRC 3.10 FlowGraph.py:545 word for word. Every number the oracle depends on is stated in the instruction (fs, noise standard deviation, band 6-18 kHz, Hann window, 2.4 kHz transition, tone 12.6 kHz at 0.316, step 1/32, x32 codes, file names and float type). The instruction gives the symptom without naming the fix, and the reference RMS / noise-band checks hold across 11 noise seeds. Valid alternative solutions I wrote all passed V5: an Embedded Python rounding quantizer, a 6-bit saturating version, codes from a separate Float To Short path, and codes via Float To Int. Truncation, floor and a 1/64 step are rejected. Problems: (F1, medium) the f2p checks measure only the power of the quantization-noise floor, not the rounding itself. A flowgraph with no quantizer, using additive uniform noise of amplitude 1/64, passes V5, and so does a mid-rise quantizer, although the instruction requires rounding to multiples of 1/32 and integer codes. Smaller issues: (F2) truncation is rejected only by the p2p RMS checks, with a 0.9% margin; (F3) the codes.dat 20-24 kHz floor is not checked; (F4) copying the injected id unchanged counts toward the hallucinated-block rate. Scratch evidence is in WSL /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-08/ (alt_fake_noise.grc, alt_epy_midrise.grc, alt_epy_trunc.grc, alt_epy_round.grc, alt_epy_sat6.grc, alt_codes_parallel.grc, alt_codes_int.grc, seed_*.grc, with .json ladder results).

findings.claim: The fail-to-pass oracle never checks that samples are actually rounded to multiples of 1/32, even though the instruction requires it ('every sample is rounded to the nearest multiple of 1/32', codes are 'the integer quantization levels'). It only measures the power of the noise floor, so two flowgraphs that do no rounding at all pass V5: (a) the missing quantizer swapped for additive uniform noise, and (b) a mid-rise quantizer whose outputs are never multiples of 1/32. The six_bit_floor spec_property says 'quantized.dat is rounded to multiples of 1/32', but its check (band_fraction 0-4 kHz and 20-24 kHz) cannot see the difference.
findings.evidence: Scratch files are in WSL ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-08/, each run with ./gb ladder <file> --task items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-08/task.json. (a) alt_fake_noise.grc replaces 'quantizer' with blocks_add_xx(float) plus analog_noise_source_x(GR_UNIFORM, amp 1.0/64, seed 3) on input 1, so nothing is quantized and codes.dat is not integer-valued. Result: highest V5, first_failed None. Values: out 0-4 kHz 2.50e-4, out 20-24 kHz 2.53e-4, codes 0-4 kHz 2.50e-4, codes rms 7.504, out rms 0.2345, peak 12600 Hz, noise band 0.0299. (b) alt_epy_midrise.grc is an Embedded Python quantizer (floor(x*32)+0.5)/32, so codes are half-integers. Result: highest V5, first_failed None (floor shares 2.50e-4 / 2.54e-4, codes rms 7.509). A model that does not know channels_quantizer could plausibly model quantization as additive uniform noise of power step^2/12, and that answer is accepted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an exactness check on codes.dat in group f2p, linked to six_bit_floor/codes_quantized. For example, add a feature to oracles.py such as 'max_frac_dev' = max|x - round(x)| (pass if <= 1e-3), or 'integer_fraction' with min 0.999. Running it on codes.dat after the skip enforces both 'multiple of 1/32' and 'integer levels'. Re-run the gates; the 4 variants all produce exact integer codes, so they should still pass. If adding a feature is not possible before pre-registration, state in spec_properties and review.notes that rounding is checked only statistically and that additive-noise or mid-rise answers are accepted.

findings.claim: The oracle does reject a truncating quantizer, which the instruction rules out ('rounded to the nearest'), but only through the pass-to-pass RMS checks, with a 0.9% margin and in the wrong group. None of the three f2p quantization checks rejects truncation. The failure is therefore reported as a broken 'signal_level'/'codes_scale' that previously held, not as a wrong repair, which misleads per-group analysis and partial credit. A truncating cast is a plausible mistake, e.g. astype(np.int16) or int() in an Embedded Python block.
findings.evidence: alt_epy_trunc.grc (np.trunc(x*32)/32) reaches V4 and fails V5. All f2p checks pass: out 0-4 kHz 3.20e-4, out 20-24 kHz 3.27e-4, codes 0-4 kHz 3.20e-4, all inside [1.23e-4, 4.92e-4]. Only the p2p checks fail: out rms 0.22097 vs lower limit 0.22296 (0.23469*0.95), and codes rms 7.0710 vs lower limit 7.1347. The bias comes from truncation toward zero and does not depend on the seed (10 noise seeds move the reference rms by about 1%). Widening the amplitude tolerance (e.g. to the common +-10%) would let truncation pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an f2p check that separates rounding from truncation, e.g. an rms check on quantized.dat with rel_tol 0.03 (correct solutions over 10+ seeds give 0.2324-0.2347, truncation gives 0.2210), linked to six_bit_floor. Alternatively note in spec_properties that the signal_level/codes_scale p2p checks also enforce rounding, so the tolerance is not widened later.

findings.claim: The instruction requires that 'both outputs' show only the 6-bit floor outside the tone and noise band. For codes.dat only the 0-4 kHz band is checked; the 20-24 kHz band is checked only on quantized.dat. One stated behaviour is therefore only partly checked.
findings.evidence: In task.json oracle.checks the band_fraction checks are: out 0-4000, out 20000-24000, codes 0-4000. There is no codes 20000-24000 check. The codes_quantized spec_property text covers only 'the same rounding-noise floor'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the matching band_fraction check on codes.dat for 20-24 kHz (same expect/min/max as the out check, group f2p, property codes_quantized), or reword the instruction to say the floor requirement applies to quantized.dat.

findings.claim: This is a nonexistent_block repair, so a model that returns the start graph unchanged is reported as hallucinating 'blocks_quantizer_ff', a block id the item itself injected. That inflates the hallucinated-block rate (a headline metric for RQ2/H2b) with copied ids rather than hallucinated ones.
findings.evidence: ./gb ladder items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-08/start.grc returns first_failed V2 with error "unknown block id 'blocks_quantizer_ff' (block 'quantizer')" and hallucinated_blocks ['blocks_quantizer_ff'] (_worker.py lines 57-85). task.json records fault.wrong_id = 'blocks_quantizer_ff', so the scorer could tell the two cases apart, but no aggregation code does so yet (no other use of 'hallucinated' in src/).
findings.suggested_fix: In the metric aggregation for repair tasks, leave out fault.wrong_id from the hallucinated-block rate when it is copied unchanged, and count it as 'fault not repaired'. Or document the convention in the item notes so the team decides once for all nonexistent_block items.
